data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when the test is installed before the subject's guard registry is populated; after the registry is populated, the test describes the registry's verdicts, and the 1-of-9 loss occurs because compile.py's shown-to-fail-first order bypasses the empty-registry state.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If all guards in the ordinarily-guarded modules are lazy, the import-time claim fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation was lost because the test file itself was not run, the registry order is irrelevant.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py's installation order is not deterministic, the observed distribution is not a stable property.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The installation ritual determines whether the test sees an unguarded subject (constraint) or an already-guarded subject (description). Shown-to-fail-first installation means the mutation is planted before the test runs, but if the subject's guard registry is populated at import time, the test never sees the unguarded failure mode. The distribution 1/9 lost vs 4/4 to 6/7 guarded reflects how many subjects have import-time guard registration versus lazy guard registration.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
